value.rationale: Choosing the locations of fixed competing opinions on a finite social interaction circle is a natural design variable, and sustained deviations in aggregate opinion share incur convex costs. A strict convex-order ranking resolves all such costs simultaneously, including variance, asymmetric convex loss, and risk-sensitive extremes, at every finite integer size. It meaningfully strengthens isolated moment formulas and identifies unique optimal and worst spacing multisets. Limitations to alternating fixed opinions and stationary counts are explicit.
